instructions: Rinse the 2 cups rice in a bowl of cold water, swishing it with your hand and pouring off the cloudy water, until it runs nearly clear, 3 or 4 changes. Cover it with fresh water and leave it to soak for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the spice paste. Break a 2 inch piece off the cinnamon stick and save the small piece. Grind the 2 inch piece with the 1 tsp fennel seeds, 1/2 tsp peppercorns, 6 of the cloves and the 3 cardamom pods to a fine powder in a spice grinder or with a mortar and pestle. Peel the ginger and the 5 garlic cloves and pound or blend them into the powder with the 3 tbsp yogurt to a smooth paste.

Cut the chicken into 2 inch pieces. In a bowl, stir them together with the spice paste, 1/2 tsp of the salt, the 1/4 tsp turmeric and the 1/2 tsp Kashmiri chili powder until every piece is coated. Leave it on the counter while you chop.
Thinly slice the onion. Chop the tomato. Chop 1/4 cup of the mint and 1/4 cup plus 2 tbsp of the cilantro. Thinly slice the green chili into a small bowl for the table.

Heat the 3 tbsp oil in a large heavy pot with a tight lid over medium. Add the small piece of cinnamon, the remaining 2 cloves, the star anise and the bay leaf. After about 20 seconds they'll sizzle and smell warm. That's your cue for the onion.
Add the onion and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's evenly golden.
Add the chicken with all its marinade. Cook over medium for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until the outside of the pieces turns pale and opaque.
Stir in the tomato, the chopped mint and 1/4 cup of the cilantro. Cover and cook over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until the tomato is mushy.
Uncover, turn the heat to medium and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until the liquid has cooked off and the oil shows at the edges.
Meanwhile, pour the can of coconut milk and 1 3/4 cups water into a saucepan with the remaining 3/4 tsp salt and heat it until it's steaming. That should be about 3 1/2 cups.
Drain the rice well. Pour the hot coconut milk into the pot with the chicken and bring it to a boil. Add the rice and stir it gently once so it sits in an even layer.
Boil it uncovered over medium for 6 to 8 minutes, without stirring, until the liquid has dropped below the top of the rice and you see small holes on the surface.
Put the lid on, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 15 minutes. No peeking.
Turn off the heat and leave the pot covered for 15 minutes.
Taste a little of the rice. If it's flat, sprinkle a pinch more salt over the top before you fluff it.

Fluff the rice gently with a fork, lifting the chicken up from the bottom, and scatter the last 2 tbsp of the cilantro over the top. Serve with the rest of the yogurt and the sliced green chili on the side.
method_notes: Both read versions marinate chicken in yogurt with a Chettinad spice blend, cook it into fried onions and tomato with whole spices, then cook soaked rice right in the same pot. Swasthi's Recipes (the lead) grinds fennel, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom with ginger and garlic into the marinade, adds mint and cilantro with the tomato, dries it off and cooks 2 cups of rice in 3 1/2 cups of hot thin coconut milk, then rests it for 15 minutes. Simple Indian Meals uses a ready Chettinad masala, adds star anise, black cardamom and peppercorns to the oil and cooks it under pressure with only a little coconut milk. This follows the lead's pot method and liquid ratio for 4, adding the star anise and black pepper from Simple Indian Meals for the Chettinad flavor, and keeps the green chili on the side.
